newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul blames Japan's political party over islands.
newsitem.headline: Seoul blames Japan's political party over islands.

text.p: South Korea accused Japan's Liberal Democratic Party on Tuesday of acting irresponsibly by including in its party platform an assertion of sovereignty over a group of tiny islands also claimed by Seoul.

A foreign ministry statement also denounced a decision by the largest Japanese political party to adopt in the general election platform a controversial call for official cabinet minister visits to Tokyo's Yasukuni war shrine.

"The Liberal Democratic Party is taking an irresponsible stance as a public party by claiming ownership of Tokdo, which is part of Korea's traditional territory historically and under international laws, and by making an unprecedented decision to adopt this in its election platform," the statement said.
"We will by no means forgive this," it said. The platform was issued late on Monday.
Japanese right-wing officials sparked Korean outrage by laying claim to the rocky islands, known as Tokdo in Korea and Takeshima in Japan.
Seoul has already begun to improve a wharf on the rocky islands, under guard by South Korean security forces.

Calling the Yasukuni war memorial a "shrine of war criminals", the South Korean statement said the Liberal Democratic Party's decision to push for official shrine visits in its election platform was aimed at justifying Japan's agression during World War Two.
"We cannot accept this," the South Korean statement said. "The government will sternly deal with Japan's claim for ownership of Tokdo and the Yasukuni Shrine visits."

Japan has claimed sovereignty of the islands since 1905 when it signed an agreement with Korea that paved the way for colonisation. Korea says its claims to the island date back to the year 512 and are well-documented.
The barren outcrops cover a total land area of only 250 square metres (299 square yards), but the waters around them are rich in fishery resources and possibly underwater minerals.

South Korea and Japan normalised ties in 1965, but bilateral relations have never been cordial because of Koreans' bitter memories of atrocities committed during Tokyo's harsh 1910-45 colonial rule over the peninsula.
Japan is currently locked in a bitter sovereignty dispute with Chinese communities in Hong Kong, China, Taiwan and Macau over a separate group of islands in the East China Sea.
A Hong Kong activist died in stormy waters near the isles during an anti-Japanese protest last week.
